name: CHIRPS 2.0
provider: UC Santa Barbara Climate Hazards Center
typical_latency: final ~3 weeks after the month; preliminary ~2–5 days
about: Satellite infrared rainfall blended with rain-gauge reports, 1981 to present. The reference for this tracker: climatology (1993–2016), bias correction and verification all use CHIRPS. The final record ends with the last complete month; preliminary daily files fill the days after it.
note: final record to 2026-09-30, preliminary days after

name: ARC2
about: Africa Rainfall Climatology v2: Meteosat infrared cloud-top temperatures merged with daily GTS rain-gauge reports. Quick and long record; tends to miss light rain and shows occasional single-cell spikes.

name: TAMSAT v3.1
about: Africa-only rainfall from Meteosat thermal-infrared cold-cloud duration, calibrated against historical gauges. Good at telling rain from no rain; weaker for heavy amounts.

name: PDIR-Now
about: Precipitation from infrared imagery by a neural network (PERSIANN family), near-global, quasi-real-time. Fastest product here; no gauge correction.

name: IMERG Late (V07)
about: Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM: passive-microwave rainfall from the GPM constellation, gaps filled with infrared; the Late run has more microwave overpasses than Early. Fetched as a Kenya subset through NASA's cloud OPeNDAP (Earthdata login).

name: IMERG Early (V07)
about: Same algorithm as IMERG Late, issued sooner with fewer satellite overpasses; for monitoring when speed matters.

name: IMERG via Earth Engine
about: Half-hourly IMERG summed to daily in Google Earth Engine; an alternative route when NASA servers are unreachable.

name: GSMaP Gauge (operational v8)
about: Global Satellite Mapping of Precipitation: microwave + infrared rainfall adjusted to the CPC gauge analysis. Needs an Earth Engine project (or a JAXA G-Portal account) before it can be downloaded.

name: ECMWF ensemble (ENS)
about: 51-member ensemble, 15 days. The maps show the member median; the planting-rain chances use all 50 perturbed members.

name: GDPS
about: Canada's Global Deterministic Prediction System (GEM model), 10 days.

name: ICON
about: Germany's ICOsahedral Nonhydrostatic global model, 7.5 days on the open-data server.

name: UKMO Global
about: Met Office Unified Model global deterministic forecast on AWS open data, 7 days used here.

name: ECMWF SEAS5
typical_latency: new start every month, published on the 5th
about: Seasonal ensemble (25 members for the forecast, hindcasts 1993–2016), bias-corrected against CHIRPS; observed CHIRPS replaces the forecast up to the latest observed day.
note: observations spliced in to 2026-10-25; next start 1 Nov, published 5 Nov
